purpose: Map LIVE scientific arguments (contested questions with identifiable camps in the literature) to the repo datasets, genome tiers and knowledge-graph records that could settle them. An entry here is NOT a finding and NOT a registered prediction: it is a candidate for one. Promotion discipline: candidate -> Delphi-score its probability (recorded on the problem-graph edge, per the 2026-10-26 record-every-action rule) -> register the prediction before scoring -> resolution record -> nanopub.
selection_rule: An argument qualifies only if (a) at least two identifiable camps disagree in print, (b) at least one repo dataset bears on it, (c) the species has genome tier A or B (assembly + gene annotation; see organism census), and (d) a named measurement or public record could in principle settle it. Arguments the literature has already settled are excluded or marked partly_settled with the live remainder stated.

genome_tiers.A: assembly + curated annotation + UniProt protein states + expression/phenotype atlas + mutant literature (Danio rerio GRCz11/ZFIN, Drosophila melanogaster BDGP6/FlyBase, Xenopus tropicalis UCB_Xtro_10/Xenbase, Mus musculus GRCm39/MGI)
genome_tiers.B: assembly + gene models, thin atlas/mutant layer (e.g. Bos taurus ARS-UCD2.0, Astyanax, Gasterosteus)
genome_tiers.D: no DNA (fossil bracketing only) -- excluded from this map

arguments.question: How is the zebrafish BMP dorsoventral gradient formed: Chordin-mediated shuttling, regulated free diffusion/source-sink, or ECM/HSPG-shaped diffusion?
arguments.settled_part: Repo prediction ZF-TUR-01 (scored 2026-10-26): free-diffusion size prior D_chd/D_bmp2b = 0.759 (mature-chain 0.51) is violated by published evidence; Chordin-mediated transport is required. Remaining live part: does the BMP signalling range SCALE across Danio species of different embryo size, and by which of the above mechanisms?

camps.claim: BMP is transported as a BMP-Chordin complex and released by Tolloid cleavage; gradient shape is set by the shuttle, not by free BMP diffusion.
camps.representative_evidence: Zinski et al. 2017 (systems model of zebrafish BMP gradient formation); Pomreinke et al. 2017 (Sog/Chordin shuttling in the sister Drosophila system); repo ZF-TUR-01/ZF-TUR-02 resolution records

camps.claim: Spatially regulated production, diffusion and receptor-mediated clearance can generate the observed gradient without obligatory long-range shuttling at every stage.
camps.representative_evidence: Source-sink modelling literature on zebrafish gastrula BMP patterning; effective-mobility measurements that vary by stage and tissue

camps.claim: Extracellular matrix and heparan-sulfate proteoglycans dominate effective BMP mobility, making both pure-diffusion and pure-shuttle accounts incomplete.
camps.representative_evidence: HSPG/ECM perturbation studies of BMP distribution in fish and fly embryos

arguments.settling_measurement: Paired FRAP/effective-mobility measurements of tagged BMP and Chordin plus pSmad1/5 gradient ranges in at least two Danio species of different embryo size, under identical staging.

candidate_prediction.statement: Across Danio species, pSmad gradient range scales with embryo DV extent while free BMP mobility does not; the scaling variable is Chordin/Tolloid flux, so species with relatively larger chd expression domains show disproportionately longer BMP ranges.
candidate_prediction.falsifier: BMP range is invariant across species once embryo size is normalised, or scales with measured free-BMP mobility instead of Chordin-domain size.
candidate_prediction.confidence_basis: Zebrafish half decidable from public pSmad/FRAP records (as ZF-TUR-01 was); cross-species mobility series does not yet exist as a table and likely needs literature extraction or new measurement.

priority.rank_note: Highest-value live remainder of an argument the repo has already partly settled; do not re-litigate the settled half.

arguments.question: Are zebrafish stripes (and fish pigment patterns generally) a Turing reaction-diffusion system, or a cell-interaction network that only mimics one?

camps.claim: Pigment patterns arise from interacting diffusible signals with differential diffusion; wavelength is set by signal kinetics and should shift predictably when kinetics change.
camps.representative_evidence: Kondo and coworkers' reaction-diffusion analyses of fish stripe formation and regeneration; wavelength changes in pattern mutants read as kinetic changes

camps.claim: Stripes are generated by direct interactions among melanophores, xanthophores and iridophores (contact-dependent survival, repulsion, long projections); no diffusible Turing pair is required and the 'wavelength' is a cell-behaviour emergent.
camps.representative_evidence: Singh & Nusslein-Volhard and coworkers on zebrafish pigment-cell interactions; iridophore-led stripe organisation; connexin (leopard) and csf1ra (pfeffer) mutant analyses

species.name: Danio rerio (+ congeners); Bos/Equus as mammalian outgroup tests

arguments.settling_measurement: Stripe wavelength and regeneration kinetics in cell-interaction mutants (leopard/gja5b, pfeffer/csf1ra) compared quantitatively against both model classes fitted on the same fish; the Turing account must predict the wavelength shift from a kinetic parameter, the cell account from interaction ranges.

candidate_prediction.statement: Across Danio species and the leopard mutant, stripe wavelength correlates with pigment-cell interaction ranges (projection length, iridophore spacing) and NOT with any morphogen size/diffusion prior derivable from candidate Turing-pair sequences.
candidate_prediction.falsifier: Wavelength shifts are quantitatively predicted by a two-signal kinetic fit whose parameters are independently measured, while cell-interaction ranges stay constant.
candidate_prediction.confidence_basis: Mutant phenotypes and much cell-behaviour data are public (ZFIN + primary literature); a head-to-head quantitative fit on identical specimens has not been published and is the missing piece.

priority.rank_note: The repo's Bos dataset already shows the morphometric side can kill a Turing claim; this extends the same test to the system the Turing camp actually defends.

arguments.question: Is vertebrate digit patterning a BMP-SOX9-WNT Turing system modulated by Hox dose, or a positional-gradient system in which Turing-like periodicity is secondary?

camps.claim: A BMP-SOX9-WNT reaction-diffusion network generates the periodic digit pattern; Hox genes modulate its wavelength, explaining digit number changes in Hox mutants.
camps.representative_evidence: Raspopovic et al. 2014, Science (BSW Turing network in mouse digit patterning); wavelength phenotypes of Gli3/Hox compound mutants

camps.claim: Digit identities and much of the pattern are specified by positional information (Shh/Hox gradients); periodic condensation is a downstream mechanical/aggregation readout, not the pattern generator.
camps.representative_evidence: Sheth et al. 2012, Science (Hox dose and digit pattern); classical positional-information analyses of the limb bud

arguments.settling_measurement: Digit wavelength (condensation spacing) as a function of distal Hox dose in allelic series, tested against the BSW prediction that wavelength -- not just digit identity -- shifts continuously with Hox-modulated parameters.

candidate_prediction.statement: In published Hox/Gli3 allelic-series limb data, condensation spacing varies continuously and monotonically with Hox dose in the direction the BSW model requires; a pure positional account predicts identity changes at constant spacing.
candidate_prediction.falsifier: Spacing is dose-invariant while identities change, or spacing changes stepwise at identity boundaries.
candidate_prediction.confidence_basis: Phenotype series are public (MGI + primary papers) but spacing is rarely tabulated as a continuous variable; decidable by extraction, possibly only partly.

priority.rank_note: Mus was the prediction registry's named runner-up species; this is its strongest live argument.

arguments.question: How is Hedgehog transported: extracellular diffusion (with Dispatched/Scube hand-off) or cytoneme-mediated delivery?

camps.claim: Lipidated Hh is released via Dispatched/Scube-type mechanisms and moves extracellularly; gradient range is set by release, extracellular carriers and reception.
camps.representative_evidence: Vertebrate Shh release and neural-tube/limb gradient literature; effective-range measurements of lipidated vs unlipidated Hh (repo DM-HH-01, XT-SHH-01 records)

camps.claim: Signalling filopodia (cytonemes) deliver Hh directly between producing and receiving cells; apparent diffusion signatures are secondary to cytoneme dynamics.
camps.representative_evidence: Sanders et al. 2013, Nature (Drosophila cytonemes in Hh gradient formation) and subsequent cytoneme imaging studies

species.name: Drosophila melanogaster / Danio rerio / Xenopus tropicalis

arguments.settling_measurement: Gradient range after cytoneme disruption that leaves secretion intact (and vice versa), in the same tissue, with the lipidation state of the transported species verified from sequence/protein state.

candidate_prediction.statement: In the fly wing disc, disrupting cytonemes shortens the Hh signalling range (ptc domain) by a larger factor than it changes total secreted Hh, while in the vertebrate neural tube the same class of disruption leaves range largely intact (diffusion/hand-off dominant) -- i.e. the answer is taxon-specific, not universal.
candidate_prediction.falsifier: Both systems respond identically to cytoneme disruption, supporting a single universal transport mode.
candidate_prediction.confidence_basis: ZF-HH-01 already scored only partially_resolved: lipidation facts are decidable from records, gradient-shape outcomes under transport perturbation are not tabulated publicly in comparable form.

priority.rank_note: Genuinely live but the least decidable from public records; likely needs an experimental collaborator rather than literature scoring.

arguments.question: Does somite size scale with segmentation-clock period via wavefront speed (clock-and-wavefront), and what sets the scaling across species?

camps.claim: Somite length = clock period x wavefront regression speed; species differences and experimental period changes should move somite size proportionally when wavefront speed is controlled.
camps.representative_evidence: Classical clock-and-wavefront literature and cross-species clock comparisons (e.g. human vs mouse segmentation-clock period studies); repo clock_wavefront datasets in Danio/Xenopus

camps.claim: Somite size is jointly set by presomitic-mesoderm growth, axis elongation and clock properties; period alone does not predict size once growth is accounted for.
camps.representative_evidence: PSM growth and axis-elongation analyses arguing period-size correlations break under growth perturbation

arguments.settling_measurement: Paired clock-period and somite-length measurements with PSM length/wavefront speed recorded in the same embryos, across at least the fish and frog systems the repo holds.

candidate_prediction.statement: With wavefront speed controlled from published axis-elongation data, somite length / clock period is constant within each species but the proportionality differs between Danio and Xenopus by the ratio of their wavefront speeds -- a two-point scaling test the current piecemeal literature has not assembled.
candidate_prediction.falsifier: Period changes (genetic or temperature) move somite size off the wavefront-corrected proportionality in either species.
candidate_prediction.confidence_basis: Both repo rows (ZF-CLK-01, XT-CLK-01) scored partially_resolved for exactly the missing paired series; the argument stays live because that series has never been assembled in one place.

priority.rank_note: The repo already knows precisely which table is missing; assembling it is the finding.

arguments.question: How does the Dpp/BMP gradient scale with the growing Drosophila wing disc: degradation-mediated scaling, expansion-repression, or growth-coupled production?

camps.claim: Gradient length scales because effective degradation/clearance changes with tissue size; measured Dpp kinetics (Kicheva et al. 2007) plus size-dependent turnover explain scaling.
camps.representative_evidence: Kicheva et al. 2007, Science (Dpp gradient formation kinetics); Wartlick et al. 2011, Science (Dpp gradient scaling with wing-disc growth)

camps.claim: An expander molecule produced under Dpp control feeds back on gradient range, giving robust scaling that pure kinetics cannot; candidate expanders and feedback topologies remain disputed.
camps.representative_evidence: Expansion-repression modelling and candidate-expander (e.g. Pentagone) literature following Ben-Zvi and coworkers

arguments.settling_measurement: Dpp gradient length, disc size, Dpp turnover and candidate-expander expression measured across growth stages/genotypes in one quantitative series; the two camps predict different couplings between turnover and length.

candidate_prediction.statement: Across published growth-stage series, the Dpp decay length scales with disc size while measured Dpp half-life changes in the direction and magnitude the kinetics camp requires; if half-life is size-invariant, the feedback/expansion camp wins by elimination.
candidate_prediction.falsifier: Half-life and decay length decouple across stages (length scales, turnover does not), falsifying the pure-kinetics account.
candidate_prediction.confidence_basis: Core kinetics and scaling papers are public and quantitative; DM-DPP-01 showed the repo-side sequence facts (mature chain 132 aa) are already decidable in-repo at conf 0.95.

priority.rank_note: Best decidability-to-contestation ratio on this map; recommended first promotion to registration.

arguments.question: Is the bioelectric (Vmem) prepattern instructive for Xenopus craniofacial/orientation patterning -- upstream information that biochemical gradients read out -- or a downstream correlate of conventional pathways?

camps.claim: Spatial Vmem patterns, set by ion channels and gap junctions, encode target morphology and can respecify craniofacial/orientation outcomes when manipulated, upstream of gene expression changes.
camps.representative_evidence: Cervera-Levin-Mafe modelling and Levin-lab Xenopus craniofacial Vmem studies; repo flagship 2021-Cervera-Levin-Mafe reproduction and xenopus datasets

camps.claim: Apparent bioelectric effects reduce to conventional signalling (BMP/Wnt/Shh, ion-sensitive but conventional transduction); Vmem is a correlate or modulator, not an independent information layer.
camps.representative_evidence: Mainstream developmental-biology critiques requiring molecular intermediates for Vmem phenotypes; repo embryo-blind programme, whose neighbour-prediction tests scored negatively (Xenopus LOOO AUC 0.484)

arguments.settling_measurement: Blinded, pre-registered ion-channel misexpression with BMP-pathway transcriptional readout and craniofacial scoring, where the bioelectric account predicts the readout change in advance and the conventional account predicts none without direct pathway manipulation. The repo's own blind-test contract (hash-locked, scorer refuses on mismatch) is the required format, given its earlier negative blind results.

candidate_prediction.statement: Under the repo's blinded contract, targeted Vmem perturbation changes bmp4/nog expression domains in the predicted direction at an effect size the conventional-primacy account does not predict; orientation geometry is controlled with ground-truth imaging (the confound that sank the earlier Xenopus blind test).
candidate_prediction.falsifier: No directional expression change under blinded scoring, or the effect vanishes when geometry is ground-truth controlled.
candidate_prediction.confidence_basis: Not decidable from public records alone: the repo's prior blind tests in this programme were negative, so an honest prior is low and a wet-lab collaborator is required. Included because the argument is live and the repo is unusually invested in it -- with its negative history stated, not hidden.

priority.decidability: low from records, medium with collaborator
priority.rank_note: Only entry where the settling measurement is an experiment rather than a literature assembly; promotion requires an experimental partner.
